title: Database Models and Schemas
subtopics: Separating database models from API schemas
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of database models and schemas in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to defining database models.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers database models and schemas within database integration. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use database models and schemas to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is data integrity, transaction boundaries, schema evolution and bounded database access.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Database Models and Schemas matters because it is part of database integration. In practice, focus on data integrity, transaction boundaries, schema evolution and bounded database access. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Defining database models
items.text: Apply defining database models against a disposable database and synthetic data first. Make transaction ownership and cleanup explicit, parameterize values, and verify constraints and behavior after failures before considering a deployment.

items.title: Primary keys and unique constraints
items.text: Use primary keys and unique constraints as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Field types and nullability
items.text: For field types and nullability, define the accepted shape and constraints explicitly. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, distinguish omitted values from explicit nulls, and return only fields the caller is allowed to see.

items.title: Relationships and foreign keys
items.text: Use relationships and foreign keys as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run with fastapi dev main.py; use /docs to submit a valid and an invalid body.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Defining database models”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Database Models and Schemas”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Defining database models” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Database Models and Schemas, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Database Models and Schemas belongs to the broader goal of data integrity, transaction boundaries, schema evolution and bounded database access.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
